utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Lukic, is the Defence ready to present its final argument?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning to everyone. The Prosecution has made clear that they consider General Ratko Mladic guilty, but this is according to their view of how someone should be tried for war crimes. This view attempts to establish new rules for assessing guilt and started with the proclamation first stated in the indictment in paragraph 12 that makes it clear how the Prosecution defines guilt. If someone is a member of the JNA, the Serbian police, Serbian authorities, or a member of the Bosnian Serb government, Bosnian Serb police structures, Bosnian Serb municipal structures, the VRS, or just a local Bosnian Serb, then you are automatically guilty of being part of a JCE, which includes two separate genocides. Later it was pointed out by the Defence that this literally applied to every local Bosnian Serb over the age of 16, which the Prosecution did not ever contradict, deny, or correct. This definition of guilt has always been ever-present in the background of the Prosecution's case and in how they interpret the evidence. Thus, according to the Prosecution, General Ratko Mladic is already guilty at the moment the indictment is signed because he is a soldier and an officer in first the JNA and later the VRS. He is guilty per the Prosecution just because he is a Serb and tried to defend his country, first Yugoslavia and then Republika Srpska, from attacks and war that were started and pursued by others, not by Serbs. The Prosecution wants to assert strict liability for everyone who is Serbian and everyone who had any position within legitimate Serb government, civilian and military organs. This is nothing more than impermissible collective guilt. They would have General Mladic stand to be on trial for the crimes of the Serb people, as perceived by the Prosecution. We must stress that the Prosecution case, at least how it is now presented in their final brief, which is not how it was presented in the indictment, is that General Ratko Mladic is guilty for things that occurred in Bosnia-Herzegovina prior to his becoming commander of the VRS Main Staff on May the 12th, 1992. Again, this betrays that the true essence of the Prosecution's motive is to convict General Mladic because he is a Serb, because he acted in accordance with the domestic laws and his duty and obligations to serve in his country's army to defend its people from a war being prepared and pursued against them, both on a local level and on the international plain. If that is the appropriate standard of proof - that is to say, if being a Serb and a member of the JNA and later VRS defending his country and its people against an armed enemy that used ethnic and religious fanaticism to try and take power - then General Mladic is guilty. And guilty alongside General Mladic is every single military officer that has ever served in any country's army in the entire world. That is the absurd [sic] that ultimately would come from the Prosecution's tactic of selectively presenting the evidence and attempting to alter the way burden of proof works for criminal justice. It is our job today and in the next few days to remind Your Honours and remind the public, of which the non-Serbian portion of the public have perhaps already convicted our client in their minds upon reading of the indictment, that the Prosecution's indictment and policy of collectively blaming all Serbs of being part of a JCE and then blaming General Ratko Mladic for all crimes ever committed by any Serbs, known or unknown, is inappropriate. Later we will discuss the appropriate standards and how burden of proof is supposed to function and demonstrate that under the appropriate standard, this Prosecution has failed to meet that burden and, thus, Ratko Mladic is not guilty. But first, now I want to remind everyone that Your Honours will judge Ratko Mladic, but history will judge these proceedings and you as Judges for what verdict you came back with. History will judge if justice was done and seen to be done, or if shortcuts were taken and if the Prosecution is permitted to rely on propaganda, faulty evidence, and the wrong standard to convict Ratko Mladic because he is already deemed guilty by many. Indeed, this is the first time in my career as a lawyer over 33 years now, that I stand before three Judges where two of the Judges have already in prior cases explicitly found my client guilty before he even was on trial and without the ability to defend himself. It is the first time that I stand before a Trial Chamber where its staff have come over in part from another case having already convicted my client there too, again, without giving him the ability to defend himself, because he was not on trial yet. It is your obligation and duty to set aside the prejudicial view that you may have from these prior cases and focus on this evidence in this case, not what the Prosecution wants it to be or what you remember it to be from those prior cases. I hope that you can set aside as professional Judges that pre-judging and rule fairly and in accord with the evidence in this case. Some of your decisions worry us that this may not be the case, especially when recently you confirmed that you did not see it as a problem that you had already started work on the judgement even before final briefs were filed. History will judge what is done in this courtroom. Indeed, these and other things that transpired during the trial have shocked legal professionals from around the world because procedures are so different in this trial than they were in other ICTY trials or even in criminal trials in the rest of the world. But I remind you, as much as the ICTY has modified certain procedures, it has not modified the essential items. Article 21 ensures that General Mladic be treated equally like all other accused before this Tribunal. It also guarantees him a fair trial. Rather than focusing on the actual orders and conduct of General Ratko Mladic, the human being and person, the Prosecution in both their final brief and the submissions we have had to listen to the last week attempts to pump General Mladic to superhuman proportions and abilities as if he was all-knowing and all-powerful to see, hear and control everything and everyone in Bosnia-Herzegovina, even before he came to Republika Srpska, even before he was named commander of the Main Staff. It is our job to remind Your Honours, remind the Prosecution, and remind the public, not only watching today but future generations who will judge these proceedings as a part of history, that Ratko Mladic is a person, not a superhuman being. Ratko Mladic is an accused who stands before you an innocent man and protected by certain due process rights afforded by the ICTY Statute. He is innocent because the presumption of innocence which forces the Prosecution to prove his guilt beyond a reasonable doubt and because the evidence, which later my colleague Mr. Ivetic will painstakingly show you, demonstrates that the Prosecution has failed to overcome the presumption of innocence when the proper burden of proof analysis is applied. I wish to also remind you that context is always important and is often ignored or misstated by the Prosecution. To accept the Prosecution case, one must pretend that the Serbs or Bosnian Serb forces, as they call them, acted in a vacuum where there only existed alongside innocent Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat civilians. Can we see the next slide, please. To believe the Prosecution's vision of the case, one has to ignore the presence and activities of an opposing armed opponent consisting of multiple paramilitary organisations and armies. It is my job to remind you that General Mladic and the VRS and the people of Republika Srpska were threatened and attacked by not just the armed Patriotic League of the SDA - it's P5897, P6277, P3133 - not just the Green Berets - it's P3844, P4068, P6565 - not just the Army of B and H - P7171, D1243 - not just the Croat HVO, not just the regular Croatian army that illegally crossed over into Bosnia-Herzegovina - P482; P4922; transcript page 41103; D1661, page 37; D867; D614 - but also by the NATO alliance and UNPROFOR that took the side of these enemy forces and acted in a biased manner ultimately using deadly force to kill Serbs and destroy Serb infrastructure. If Ratko Mladic is to be judged for everything that happened in Bosnia and Herzegovina, then we have to consider everyone else that was there, that was armed, and that had a role and effect on things. In this regard, I remind you of the evidence that the Bosnian Muslim SDA was preparing for war and secretly arming and establishing the Patriotic League and Green Berets in all the municipalities of Bosnia-Herzegovina, already since 1990 and 1991, long before General Mladic came to be appointed as head of the VRS Main Staff on the 12th of May, 1992. The evidence demonstrates that the Main Staff of the Patriotic League was set up in Sarajevo with nine Regional Staffs, with 103 municipal and numerous other staffs for smaller territorial units, with a large number of units from platoon to brigade rank. By the beginning of August 1992, through these SDA activities, about 170.000 men were armed and organised in 28 brigades, 138 detachments of various purposes and 16 independent battalions. Armed members of the Patriotic League and Green Berets existed throughout the municipalities of Bosnia-Herzegovina already, as I said, in 1991. We can find it in D1870; D646; P1999, page 42; D1661, page 9. And these armed combatants did not disappear and did not just sit quietly and peacefully after General Mladic came to Bosnia-Herzegovina. Their presence and activities in Bosnia-Herzegovina are an important context for viewing the evidence and activities, events that are referred to by the Prosecution. Similarly, we have evidence that in 1992 in Posavina there were 15 brigades from Republic of Croatia which rotated or were present on this front in the critical stages of the conflict. There were also 50.000 armed members of the VHO present in Bosnia at the time of the war. D1661, page 54. I'm sorry, my colleague Ivetic just remind that I said HVO. I should have said -- yeah, HVO, I should have said HVO. Thanks. We need another slide. Let's also remember that Bosnian Muslim SDA President Alija Izetbegovic came to power on a platform advocating Islamic fundamentalism and superiority over Serbs. D1532 is a 1983 judgement, before the war, long time before the war, against Alija Izetbegovic for his activities against the SFRY at that time issued by the Sarajevo District Court. At page 14 in e-court, we see that his judgement takes into account numerous lectures and discussions where Izetbegovic promoted the following ideals: "That the goal of the Islamic revolution in our country is the creation of a unified Islamic state comprising Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, and Sandzak. "That a Jihad should be pursued to its final outcome in order to exterminate the enemy and the infidel. 'We should not wait for a challenge or a provocation. Muslims must devise that challenge themselves. They must be the ones who produce the challenge, and the goal will then disclose itself.' "That Muslims must confront all non-Muslims and communists." Izetbegovic's "Islamic Declaration" was re-published in 1991. It is in evidence as D557. Only an excerpt of that book is actually in evidence but it says enough. At page 14 in e-court: "The first and the most important of these conclusions is definitely the one about the incompatibility of Islam and existence of non-Islamic systems. There can be no peace between the Islamic faith and non-Islamic social and political infrastructures and institutions." Later Izetbegovic pronounces at page 25 of his "Islamic Declaration," I quote: "Islamic order should and can approach the overtaking of rule as soon as it is morally and numerically strong enough not only to overthrow the non-Islamic rule but develop new Islamic rule." Can we have another slide that we'll see. Then other Bosnian Muslim publications took up Izetbegovic's cause such as Vox, published in October 1992, that is in evidence under --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 1991. Sorry, 1991. That is in evidence under D580. And let's take a look not only at the translation but also the Bosnian original to see the image and what is represented. Here we have a Handzar Division Islamic soldier from World War II, that is a Nazi unit, standing on the severed heads of apparent Serb Chetniks resembling, among others, Radovan Karadzic, with the banner, "The Fourth Reich is coming, Welcome!" This particular article was met with a lot of fear and anxiety by Serbs who dreaded what was in store for them. Witness -- one of the witnesses told us about it at transcript page 24198 and further. The Vox paper was not some fringe group. It was published by the SDA local president and son of the mayor of the Sarajevo municipality who worked closely with Alija Izetbegovic, as two witnesses told us at transcript page 24198 and transcript page 23973. Another article from Vox, also October 1991, is in evidence as D558, and let's take a look at that that one. And that's the right-hand part of this PowerPoint presentation. Obituaries published for prominent Bosnian Serb political leaders in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Witness Kecmanovic told us that all these persons were alive at the time of the obituary being published. If you put this side by side by the other image as we have it now on our screens, we see that Karadzic, Koljevic and Kecmanovic resemble three of the severed heads. All of this occurred before Ratko Mladic ever set foot in Bosnia-Herzegovina in a VRS uniform. Yet certainly such things had influence upon later. Then we have the missing context of how the constitutional structure of Bosnia-Herzegovina provided equal tripartite representation for all three ethnic groups, which each having a veto power to prevent it from being discriminated against or threatened. We have it on transcript page 23807, transcript 42216, and 23806. However, the Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat parties bypassed and violated these constitutional rules to call for an illegal referendum on independence, disenfranchising the Serbs. We have that in our transcript on page 42229. We have it in P3005, pages 34 and 35; P3006, page 1; P7770, page 22; D1517, page 1; P7040, page 1. Then there is the context of how the Bosnian Muslim SDA began promoting ethnic Muslims into the MUP police beyond the established tripartite rules of equal representation and calling up reservist MUP who were Muslim while getting rid of Serb officers. We have it in P3208, pages 1 and 2; D759, pages 1 and 2; D734; P6900; P3005, page 7. Again, all of this before Ratko Mladic arrives. Still, before Ratko Mladic's arrival, we have two orders issued clandestinely by the Sarajevo SDA leadership's personnel, Hasan Efendic, the TO commander, and Alija Delimustafic, the police minister, calling upon their brethren to attack JNA convoys and attack JNA installations and lay siege to them. It's D625 and D829. We have bloody attacks by Bosnian Muslim forces upon JNA personnel a couple of days after these instructions in Sarajevo and in Tuzla, even when the same, the JNA personnel, were withdrawing peacefully and unarmed in accord with a negotiated settlement. It's P4946; D646, number 34; and D968, paragraph 22. And we have evidence of Mujahedin being brought in to fight on the side of Izetbegovic's Bosnian Muslim forces even from the ABiH, UN, and others. D1871 is ABiH source; and D2128 is UN Expert Group. D917 is a video in evidence based on footage that the Bosnian Muslim side took of its own actions. And we will see several videos now. First, we will see the establishment of Mujahedin unit, the establishment of it. Can we play it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So just as Vox magazine threatened they would do in 1991, these pictures show us. Let there be no doubt that Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina and even non-Serbs who did not go along with the SDA regime had to defend themselves for their very survival, and let's not forget that the Bosnian Muslims and Croats had threatened the survival already in World War II, the survival of Serbs, as part of the Nazi forces that terrorised Serbs, Jews and Romas in Jasenovac and other death camps. That is not to say, of course, that all Muslims were Mujahedin or that all Croats were Ustasha. Can we see the next slide, please. And let's not forget the context that Alija Izetbegovic and the leading Bosnian Muslim cleric, Reis Efendija Mustafa Ceric met to discuss how it would be beneficial for the goal of obtaining foreign intervention if a massacre were staged in Markale and also in the enclaves, with the aim that their own Muslim civilian population be sacrificed for the greater cause as Muslim martyrs. We have that evidence from the witness on page -- transcript page 42688 and onwards. This is the same Alija Izetbegovic who used the civilian population of Sarajevo as human shields, refusing to let them leave Sarajevo - we have it in P6761, page 3; D626, paragraph 63; D597, paragraph 13; D646, number 19; D597, paragraph 13 - and placing ABiH troops in civilian buildings and surrounded by civilians from which to shoot at the Serbs. D1661, paragraph 142; transcript page 25001; transcript page 25107; D613; D509, paragraph 13; D653, paragraph 38; transcript page 767, Harland; D535, paragraph 20. In the modern day, ISIS follows a similar model and acts very comparably to the words and deeds of Alija Izetbegovic and his forces, and the whole world is aligned against ISIS and still is having difficulty to stop the terror. In 1992, when Ratko Mladic came to the VRS in May, all he had to stand against the terror of Alija Izetbegovic's Mujahedin forces was a rag-tag army pulled together from remnants of various units, TO units, mobilized civilian volunteers, with not enough professional officers to effectively command and control the same. Let's remember that the Main Staff of the VRS, rather than having hundreds and thousands of officers like the JNA 2nd Military District, had just around a dozen when it started its work. But it is clear that rather than acting from some criminal purpose, the VRS and General Mladic were driven by the legitimate aim to militarily defend against these threats and attacks from a very numerous army, an enemy, who was armed and not adverse to using terror both against others and their own people to obtain the Muslim-dominated state that they had set out to obtain, as promised in Izetbegovic's Islamic Declaration. Next slide, please. And let's not forget that the Prosecution narrative ignores the words and orders of General Mladic that urge for the non-Serb civilian population to be protected and for POWs to be treated properly and in accordance with the law. Here we have words from Directive 1. It's P474, the same words we can find in D726; D961, page 1, number 1; D711, paragraph 18. Everything good and innocent that General Mladic ever uttered or signed is ignored by the Prosecution or in their final brief it is said to be a lie, because secret, unknown and undocumented alleged meetings decided another fate, as in Srebrenica, where they cannot even identify when that secret, criminal meeting would have taken place, except that it must have taken place in the few hours between two other meetings at the Fontana hotel where the evidence is that nothing improper was discussed. The Prosecution have used innuendo and impermissible inferences to say that when have you two possibilities available under the evidence, you must accept the one indicative of General Mladic's guilt, because he is General Mladic. And that is not the law, that is actually counter the law. They want you to ignore all the evidence that Ratko Mladic was consistently -- constantly seeking a cessation of hostilities and asking for the UNPROFOR to enforce compliance by the Bosnian Muslim side to agreements, which they did not. Ratko Mladic neither started nor prolonged the war. And that we have in our evidence. Can we have another slide, please. Let's not forget that the Prosecution keep talking about separation being a central part of the Serb strategic objectives and thus the alleged criminal plan and enterprise. However, if we look at the context, we see that separation was what all three ethnic parties had been negotiating with international mediators for a long time and which had been agreed to by all three sides as a way to peacefully resolve the situation and avoid the war, and that it was the Bosnian Muslim side that sabotaged these peace negotiations by going back and renouncing its signature. Again, it is Alija Izetbegovic doing this, per advice from the Americans. Ambassador Zimmermann specifically. We have it -- P6665 is a map from Ambassador Cutileiro. And we have P7772, also a map of the Cutileiro Plan from March 1992. In front of us on our screens is D1403. It's a letter to Jose Cutileiro from Karadzic, Koljevic, and Krajisnik from March the 2nd, 1992, informing him that Izetbegovic refused the plan and that at the same time and the same day, in the wedding parade in Sarajevo, a Serbian bridegroom's father was killed by a Muslim. If separation is the first step in the Serb's criminal plan, then is that also to say Ambassadors Cutileiro, Akashi, Hurd, Owen, Stoltenberg were the architects of that plan? How about other members of the international community who tried to achieve peace by way of separation? What about UNPROFOR peacekeepers trying to separate the warring parties? Are they part of the JCE, joint criminal enterprise? No, they are not. Why? Because we return to the Prosecution's central theme. It is okay if someone else does or promotes something, like separation, but if you do the same thing and you are an ethnic Serb, a member of the Bosnian Serb government, police, military, or a local Bosnian Serb, then you are automatically guilty. You are then automatically a liar if you say something else that is indicative of following the law. You are damned with guilt that you cannot wash off yourself because that guilt is made to define you by ethnicity and membership in a legitimate military organ, rather than by your acts or deeds. Vox magazine, if it were operating today, would probably react to the Prosecutor's absurd assumptions by proclaiming: "Welcome to the Fourth Reich." There is much more context that the Prosecution narrative chooses to ignore but for which there cannot be any question that Ratko Mladic is not responsible for those things, and yet they happened, and they had a profound effect on people and events in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that those uncontrollable contextual matters riled up people's emotions and tensions and that they created a threat and a powder keg all over Bosnia-Herzegovina. And that subsequent efforts to try and deal with the same cannot thus be viewed in a vacuum but they must be viewed in a context and understood according to the context. Can we have another slide. Thank you. Ratko Mladic is not a monster. He was a soldier, defending against a monster. That monster being the Islamic war machine and terror let loose by Alija Izetbegovic and his calls for Jihad, and eventually that Islamic war machine was supported by outside help, per the Prosecution's own expert, General Richard Dannatt, the US Pentagon co-ordinated NATO air-strikes to coincide with Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat military attacks to defeat Serbs. And we have it at transcript page 19188, line 19 to 19194, line 8. That is why Ratko Mladic is here today. Because he is a Serb and dared stand up against Alija Izetbegovic's Jihad which was covertly backed by the forces of NATO. Now I want to shift gears to give you a brief overview of what we will be presenting as our case theory before I hand over to Mr. Ivetic. And I will try to be brief and those things will be developed later. The Defence does not deny that unfortunate and opportunistic crimes occurred, but those in no way can be connected to General Ratko Mladic. And in any event, not every crime alleged by the Prosecution actually occurred as a crime in the manner alleged. This case still has the Prosecution seeking to hold Ratko Mladic guilty for events that have been proven under the evidence to have been the acts of the other side, Alija Izetbegovic's forces, including various shellings in Sarajevo, like Sirokaca, Markale, et cetera. This case still has the Prosecution seeking to hold Ratko Mladic guilty of destruction of cultural and religious buildings based on adjudicated facts and scant witness testimony, when the Prosecution's own expert, Riedlmayer, has confirmed that some of these mosques did not exist or were damaged or destroyed before the war. It is all an insult to the criminal justice system to be bringing charges like this. Ratko Mladic arrived as VRS commander of the Main Staff on the 12th of May, 1992. Predating that were many contextual events that gave rise to a legitimate fear, a legitimate threat, from armed Bosnian Muslim military forces sponsored by the SDA that caused a war situation to develop and explode, in which Ratko Mladic had no role. Many events in the municipalities, even crimes occurred and were pursued by others, before Ratko Mladic came to the VRS, and without any involvement of him, yet this Prosecution wants to hold him responsible. As to the interactions with others, the Prosecution has improperly recast these as illegal and secret criminal conspiracies where Mladic agreed to the JCE. But another interpretation is more logically available because these are really legitimate meetings of state organs to discuss self-defence and difficult and complex situations caused by the war. The Prosecution, by attempting to define as a JCE member every Bosnian Serb civilian, police and military member, has attempted to thus redefine every legitimate meeting as a criminal meeting. That is not appropriate. At those meetings, Ratko Mladic would speak in support of moderation and efforts for all persons of the Republika Srpska to live peacefully irrespective of ethnicity. The Prosecution would try to hold General Mladic responsible for the actions undertaken by other structures, such as police, Crisis Staffs, and other government organs, over which he had no authority and of whose actions he would not be informed. At the VRS, Ratko Mladic, when he arrived, had drastic shortages of personnel, shortages of professional officers and junior officers, and had to deal with conflicting interests and conflicting notions of how to wage a war. He, along with all other VRS officers, were excluded from the Supreme Defence Command or Council that made binding decisions for the RS. Further, civilian leaders declined to declare a state of war which further limited the powers of the army and General Mladic and his military commanders to act like an army despite the war conditions. Facing manpower shortages, sanctions, and an enemy that outnumbered him, General Mladic was further limited in terms of his abilities to effectively wage a defensive war. He did his best, trying to instill discipline, honour, and courage in his soldiers. It is instructive that not a single Prosecution witness who was a former officer of the VRS had anything negative to say about General Mladic and did not implicate him in any illegal orders. Not a single one. Even Momir Nikolic's evidence can only claim that General Mladic gave a dismissive hand gesture, not that he ordered any criminal killings. Surely if General Mladic were guilty of leading a criminal campaign, at least one insider witness would have something bad to say about him as a military officer. That is the man before you today as an accused. In the municipalities, the Prosecution sees separation of peoples and a military campaign directed against civilians to drive out or destroy all non-Serbs. But there is a more logical alternative under the evidence. Namely, the efforts in line with the Cutileiro Plan that were undertaken together by Muslims and Serb leaders in the municipalities to split the police and split the municipality, which were intended to prevent not foster war. Unfortunately, the Bosnian Muslims abandoned the efforts for peace and instead initiated attacks in municipalities and refused to disarm after same. The presence of armed Bosnian Muslim forces that did not disarm created a security risk, especially with further attacks initiated by them. These attacks and the threat of an escalated combat situation with continued fighting led many persons, both Serb and non-Serb alike, to leave the area to seek more security. The lack of jobs, resources, utilities, and food likewise made persons leave. Still others left because of orders by the SDA party or ABiH to leave an area so they could attack it or to go to another area to mobilise and strengthen ABiH forces. Persons also left when legitimate combat was undertaken to disarm these Bosnian Muslim military units and clear areas of hostile forces. Military actions were aimed at armed hostile forces and meant to separate these forces from the territory to neutralize their threat. None of this leads to the conclusion that General Mladic is criminally responsible for departures of the population or for legitimate military actions against hostile opposing forces. That military actions were tied to a legitimate military propose [sic] and not genocide against non-Serbs is best illustrated by the fact that non-Serbs who disarmed and were not hostile stayed in municipalities and not -- often were protected by the very VRS. Non-Serb personnel served in the VRS and were sought to be mobilized into VRS. Where other actions including crimes were undertaken by renegade individual VRS personnel of their own accord or non-VRS organs, such as police or paramilitaries, such actions were not under the authority of General Mladic and he cannot be criminally responsible for the same. There is no linkage between the actions and General Mladic. In the chaos of war in the municipalities, various detention facilities were set up, but most of them were operated by non-VRS organs and the accused had no role in their operation or function, and thus cannot effect conditions. Incidents, like the so-called Room 3 massacre at Keraterm, were reported as legitimate casualties from an attempted escape by the police, and thus could not be known to the accused as otherwise. As to VRS-run facilities, there were only two: Manjaca and Batkovic. As to each, the VRS orders from General Mladic were to treat POWs in accord with the law. Shortages in resources and supplies made it difficult to meet dietary and other requirements 100 per cent and the VRS asked for assistance from humanitarian aid agencies. Prisoners were registered with ICRC and known crimes against them were punished and sought to be prevented. The VRS and General Mladic had a policy of seeking always to exchange prisoners with the other side and worked with various humanitarian organisations to make that happen. None of this leads to the conclusion that General Mladic is criminally responsible for treatment in detention facilities. Again, there is no linkage with General Mladic. As to Sarajevo, contrary to the Prosecution's false image of the SRK as an aggressor against an undefined [sic] and vulnerable city of civilians, the evidence supports the alternative conclusion that legitimate and proportionate military actions were taken against a defended city that had a significant number of ABiH troops interspersed with civilians. The SRK was essentially an army of local residents inexperienced in combat who were cobbled together by necessity and held as one by the small number of professional officers in their midst and the desire to protect their homes and their families from what they perceived as a rising tide of Bosnian Muslim fanaticism and hostility unleashed by Alija Izetbegovic. The SRK and VRS had little desire to take Sarajevo. Their objectives were simpler than that: They wanted to feel that they would be safe in a territory that valued the rights of all peoples equally, in which they were free from the threat of subjugation. Their war was one of self-defence. That is how General Mladic understood the situation around Sarajevo, and that is how General Mladic intended to lead the VRS around Sarajevo, in a war of self-defence. In the context of Sarajevo, it is important to note that the legitimate combat ensued in and around Sarajevo between 1992 and 1995 was not meant to terrorise. The Serb political leaders and General Mladic negotiated cease-fires and held diplomatic talks for the resolution of the conflict, but those on the ground felt little relief. Cease-fires were constantly violated by Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, who also ignored weapons exclusion zones and did not demilitarise Sarajevo. Weapons were illicitly shipped in through humanitarian convoys for the ABiH. The SRK were attacked by ABiH mobile mortars that evaded their defensive return fire. They were harassed by ABiH artillery positions in civilian areas, sniped at from high-rise buildings, and despite their mounting frustrations and the death of civilians located within the territory they were trying to protect, they were constantly told by their superiors to hold fire unless absolutely necessary. It became a question of how much they could tolerate before it became absolutely imperative to return fire. The Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina fired in provocation and to inflict damage to the SRK from amongst Sarajevo's residential neighbourhoods and from their hiding places in residential tower blocks and the grounds of the local hospitals knowing that this limited the ability of the SRK to return fire and defend themselves and could be used to further fuel propaganda efforts of the ABiH to portray Serbs as ruthless villains. It was a constant balancing act for the SRK to determine exactly what force was required to halt these attacks and how much was too much and would unduly impact on the local civilian population in which the Army of BiH had hidden themselves. The VRS and General Mladic constantly appealed to the UN to act according to its mandate and take action against Army of BiH violations of cease-fires and violations of the rules of war, but to no avail. These frustrations were borne out of the negotiating table and in meetings with internationals, driving many, including the accused, to make threats and adopt hard-line positions they might otherwise have avoided, but always with the aim of trying to obtain a permanent cessation of hostilities rather than to enflame the war. These frustrations only grew as the international community criticised and protested and punished the actions lawfully undertaken by the SRK, wilfully ignoring the actions of the Army of BiH, both lawfully undertaken or otherwise, including the deliberate sniping and shelling of their own people, for which they often imputed blame upon the SRK, knowing that they could and would get away with it. It seemed to many at the same time like a masterful piece of manipulation of the international community by the Bosnian leadership. The evidence now reveals that, indeed, Alija Izetbegovic chose to sacrifice the lives of his own people in staged massacres which he blamed upon the VRS for sympathy and to get outside intervention on his behalf. General Mladic cannot be criminally responsible for the same. The international community asserted, and continues to try to assert, that Sarajevo was proclaimed as a safe zone. This is, quite frankly, a joke. The Muslim side launched 28 major offensives on the Serb positions within Sarajevo, as well as countless small offensives. Countless. Every day. Sarajevo was definitely a defended city and not a demilitarised zone. As to Srebrenica, the demilitarization of that locale was violated and not adhered to by both the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina forces of Naser Oric and the UN personnel who turned a blind eye to the same. The presence and attacks of Oric's forces transformed Srebrenica into a defended city rather than a demilitarised zone. The VRS Krivaja 95 action was a legitimate military action against a hostile enemy force, as was ambush and combat with the column of Srebrenica's military forces that tried to break through to Tuzla. There was no forcible transfer of the civilian population from Potocari. If the transfers from Potocari were part of a criminal plan, then those that planned it would be guilty. In this case, it was the civilian and military leadership of the Srebrenica Muslims themselves who first declared to leave, and then it was the UN that ordered Colonel Karremans to ask General Mladic to permit and assist in the evacuation in order to prevent a humanitarian disaster. To hold General Mladic criminally liable for a humanitarian action ordered by the ABiH and Bosnian Muslim civilians and ordered -- requested by UNPROFOR would be a gross perversion of justice that would forever tarnish and blemish the reputation and legacy of this Tribunal and threaten the very concept of international law and justice. As to the unfortunate killings that occurred in Srebrenica, the Defence does not deny that some persons were killed in opportunistic and uncontrollable acts of private revenge by members of the MUP, by locals, and even renegade members of the VRS security organs. These killings were not ordered by General Mladic and were not committed in direct violation of the express orders -- and were committed in direct violation of the express orders of General Mladic who was recorded at several instances and by multiple persons as having decreed that all POWs would be exchanged with the other side. The Prosecution expert, Richard Butler, confirms that he has found no express orders from General Mladic for the killings. That is because General Mladic did not order them and was not present when they occurred. General Mladic cannot be criminally responsible for the same. Now as to these killings, it must be understood that not all the deaths that are claimed by the Prosecution are the result of killings that were criminal in nature. The Prosecution does not care to differentiate between criminal deaths and those killed in a legitimate fire-fight after detainees at Kravica overpowered police guards and took their weapons, killing and wounded these guards, which precipitated the revenge killings. The Prosecution, likewise, fails to acknowledge its own expert, Butler, its own body of witness statements taken by themselves, and the fact that Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina itself shows significant number of combat casualties of the column, which numbered up to 6.000 according to the Muslim side. Rather, it includes those deaths to boost the number of victims from the criminal killings. Further, the Prosecution tried to ignore ABiH evidence and its own investigation that indicated persons exhumed from Srebrenica mass graves were casualties that had become deceased in the years prior to 1995 and thus could not be attributed as victims of crimes in 1995. Lastly, the Prosecution relies on unreliable demographic combinatory tactics to get a targeted result to further boost their number of victims. When we say that, we mean Ewa Tabeau. It was revealed at trial that 70 per cent of Prosecution's victims exhumed from Srebrenica mass graves were, in fact, registered soldiers of Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Given the lack of care taken to determine the truth forensically and serious questions raised about the Prosecution's own forensic investigation into how they died, including evidence that those leading the OTP and PHR exhumations comprised -- compromised that work - William Haglund, by destroying clothes that could have told the military status of a body, and Dr. Kirschner, by forcing pathologists to change cause of death in autopsies - it is impossible to determine with certainty how many of those persons were potentially killed in combat to the degree required to be reasonable doubt standard. This is especially true given that other questions were raised by forensic work and that the reliability of those findings. General Mladic cannot be criminally responsible for the same either. As to the claim of hostages, the Defence again must point out that under the full context of the factual evidence it is clear that UN personnel were detained as POWs and combatants after the UN engaged NATO and both came combatants in striking Serb positions, using UN personnel as the means to identify targets and direct the fighter jets to the same. The only orders of General Mladic were to treat these persons in accord with the laws as POWs. The evidence is not, for the most part -- the evidence -- sorry. The evidence is that, for the most part, VRS commanders followed General Mladic's orders and kept those individuals in proper POW conditions. In a few isolated incidents, renegade persons, and persons unknown and not acting pursuant to VRS orders, took excessive measures with detained UN personnel. In all instances, the actions of General Mladic were to respond by ordering subordinates to secure these same men in VRS custody and they were thereafter treated in accord with POW positions [sic]. Thus General Mladic cannot be held responsible for the acts of persons not following his orders but engaged in personal acts, especially when he undertook to remove those same UN personnel from harm's way and have them secured as POWs with protections afforded as flowing therefrom. Not one person was harmed and, moreover, everybody was released shortly after. As a further overview of what the Defence has shown in detail in the final brief and that we will in more detail today and the next days bring out in court, we must stress that the Prosecution must rely on unbelievable and compromised evidence to try and attain its burden to convict General Mladic. They made a deal with the devil as to Srebrenica, with Momir Nikolic, who tried to pass off his own role in crimes to General Mladic because he wanted to reduce his sentence and be released early. And he was rewarded for this by being released early. But the flaw in Nikolic's entire self-serving story is the concession that he never received any explicit orders to commit killings of Srebrenica POWs before he commenced to orchestrate the same. This means neither from General Mladic nor Colonel Blagojevic, his superior. Nikolic is present everywhere and has blood up to his elbows. Blagojevic and Mladic cannot be placed anywhere near the killings. General Mladic cannot be held criminally liable for the criminal acts of Momir Nikolic and those he conspired with to kill Srebrenica POWs, in violation of General Mladic's orders and without his knowledge. The Prosecution likewise turns to a body of purported radio relay communications -- communications intercepts that defy technology, common sense and logic. On the one hand, the most important conversations always were preserved by recording them. On the other hand, none of the alleged important conversations alleged of General Mladic can be found to have been recorded. One of the main radio intercept operators denounced by the head of the unit and by official records as having not worked there until 1996, one full year after the alleged intercepts were heard and written down by him. Intercept records were not given to the OTP until many years later. Some in books bear indicia of a date of publication after 1995 which defies logic. This questionable evidence cannot rise to the level necessary to convict anyone. The Prosecution also relies on propaganda and other evidence without regard for the potential bias of that source, including international media and members of international organisations, such as UNPROFOR and UNMOs. That there was bias amongst some of the members of UNPROFOR and UNMOs has been demonstrated and confirmed by several former UN officers who have testified at this trial. Thus no one, let alone Ratko Mladic, should be convicted based on evidence that comes from such sources prone to bias. Before I turn over these duties to my colleague Ivetic, let me just stress that as more and more evidence has come in, it has become more and more clearer how much the Prosecution has twisted and misrepresented facts. This Defence was ready and sought to provide even more evidence and witnesses that we believe would have likewise shown that Ratko Mladic cannot be guilty of the things he is charged with, but we were prevented by this Chamber from doing so, and we believe this was done unfairly, since we had not used up the time allocated to us. That error by this Chamber can be rectified only with an acquittal. So I urge you to correct that mistake. Now Mr. Ivetic will probably after the break continue with the remainder of our submissions. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Just to have matters perfectly from a procedural point of view, as you may remind, there was a discussion about Mr. Ivetic addressing -- in the 98 bis hearing to address the Court. I think at that point in time there was an issue as to whether he could address the Court in the absence of counsel, but then in 98 bis, it was established that Mr. Stojanovic as co-counsel was there. So under those circumstances, Mr. Ivetic addressed the Court though not being counsel. I think we are in a similar position now, that both lead counsel and co-counsel are present so that there -- I'll just check that with you, Mr. Tieger, there's no problem in Mr. Ivetic presenting this part of the final argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Our intent is only not to bother everybody with my accent, so you'll listen to proper English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's a very charming accent, Mr. Lukic. Then I think we'll first take a break, and resume at ten minutes to 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue with hearing the final argument, I'd like to raise one matter, Mr. Lukic, which is the following. The Defence has filed two motions seeking admission of evidence under Rule 85; that is, related to sentencing. The first motion deals with three statements; the second one with one only. The first motion, in the response by the Prosecution, there was at the very end a kind of a counter proposal if the Chamber would allow -- would admit those three documents, the Prosecution then seeks to have one document related to the evidence you are presenting to be admitted as well. The Chamber wonders whether you are going to respond to that proposal as contained in the response by the Prosecution, whether you want to respond to that or whether you leave it in the hands of the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
